newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI buys dollars to check rupee rise.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI buys dollars to check rupee rise.

text.p: The Indian rupee came off early highs in afternoon trade Monday on central bank intervention, dealers said.
They said the rupee was pinned back to around 35.80 to the dollar on Reserve Bank of India (RBI) dollar purchases after trading in a 35.795-35.805 range for most of the morning.
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted 35.797/802 rupees.

"The RBI bought at 35.795 and went up to 35.805," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "But they bought in limited amounts only. The rupee is down by about one paise at the moment. If they keep buying, maybe we will see 35.82/83 by close today."
"Otherwise if the RBI buying is not large enough, the rupee could very well retrace as dollar supplies remain good and demand from the market is poor," the dealer said.
Dealers said the RBI bought forward dollars also but the impact on premiums was minor.
"RBI bought outright June and July delivery dollars," said a dealer. "But premiums are little changed from morning levels."
July delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 24/26 paise against opening quotes of 23/25.
